newsitem.title: USA: Nynex has higher quarter against strong year ago.
newsitem.headline: Nynex has higher quarter against strong year ago.

text.p: NYNEX Corp. reported first quarter earnings a few cents ahead of expectations, excluding the effects of an enhanced pension offer and in spite of difficult comparisons to a strong period a year earlier.
The telecommunications giant had adjusted first quarter earnings of $403.1 million, or 92 cents a share, compared with $361.5 million, or 83 cents a share a year earlier.
The First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter was 90 cents a share.

The adjusted earnings excluded charges to cover an enhanced pension plan offer to employees and other one-time items in both 1997 and 1996. The latest quarter's results exclude a 56 cent per share charge to cover an enhanced pension offer to 2,900 employees, while the 1996 first quarter excluded a charge of 16 cents a share for about 960 employees who accepted the offer.
NYNEX had revenues of $3.38 billion in the first quarter of 1997, up from $3.32 billion for the 1996 period.

NYNEX said a sales "blitz" helped increase revenues for new value-added services like Caller ID, Call Waiting and voice messaging by 35.1 percent and drove up total non-usage revenues 6.0 percent, the strongest gains in over two years.
Montgomery analyst Bill Vogel said the NYNEX results were "outstanding," given difficult comparsions versus a year ago, and believes they may accelerate during the remainder of 1997.

"I am confident that the company is going to deliver solid double-digit growth in (earnings per share) for the forseeable future," Vogel said, adding that, "A strong case can be built for accelerating momentum into the balance of the year."

The company said underlying growth in subscription revenues from value-added services in addition to basic access was partially offset by a 3.3 percent decline in usage revenues over the first quarter of last year.
1996 first quarter results were aided by sky-rocketing residential call volumes during a series of winter storms.
NYNEX said robust sales of business services continued in the face of competition, with Centrex sales rising 12.9 percent and private line revenues increasing 13.1 percent.
NYNEX is awaiting approval from U.S. regulators to go ahead with its proposed merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.
NYNEX shares were up 62.5 cents to $44.625 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
